# sec-filing-ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). uv workspace of four packages, scaffolds only.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: about 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, minutes of downloading at 3 requests/s; SEC full-index and daily-index directories. Measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, weeks of downloading for the full history at 3 requests/s; index row count times request rate, not yet measured |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings handled: picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until submissions are on disk; no basis yet |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Index ingestion core
      Objective: Ingest real quarterly and daily index files into one filing-index table, at the smallest standard that gives a usable table.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (package scaffolds only)
      Produces: a queryable filing-index table built from real SEC index files; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — one table holds rows from at least one real quarterly index and the real daily indexes after it, with no duplicate filing where they overlap; the findings file records the files fetched, bytes, row count, elapsed time and request rate of the real run.
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability → Stage 4; point-in-time awareness → Stage 5; full validation suites → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submission download
      Objective: Download the individual submissions that the filing-index table's rows name.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: the filing-index table (Stage 1)
      Produces: submissions on disk, each findable from its index row; the measured download rate and volume, in the plan's Handoff
      Exit: O2 — the submissions for a real slice of index rows are on disk and each one resolves from its row; a rerun after an interruption fetches only what is missing; the measured bytes, file count and elapsed time are extrapolated to the full history.
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability → Stage 4; full validation suites → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick out the 10-K and 8-K filings from the downloaded submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: submissions on disk, findable from index rows (Stage 2)
      Produces: the extracted main documents of 10-K and 8-K filings, each linked to its index row
      Exit: O3 — for the Stage 2 slice, every 10-K and 8-K is identified, amendments included, and its main document is extracted; the filings that could not be handled are listed with a reason.
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability → Stage 4; full validation suites → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Manifests and traceability
      Objective: Make every index row, submission and extracted document traceable to the exact source bytes it came from, and rebuildable from those bytes.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening)
      Consumes: the outputs of Stages 1–3
      Produces: a manifest of retained source snapshots with content hashes and parser versions; rebuild from retained bytes without SEC requests
      Exit: each output row and document names its source snapshot and hash; a parser-version change rebuilds the outputs from retained bytes with zero SEC requests and no duplicate records.
      Leaves out: point-in-time awareness → Stage 5; full validation suites → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Point-in-time awareness
      Objective: Reconcile later changes to quarterly indexes without losing what the table said before.
      Outcomes: O1 (hardening)
      Consumes: the manifest and retained snapshots (Stage 4)
      Produces: versioned generations of the filing-index table, with a change record per generation
      Exit: re-reading a changed quarterly index produces a new generation that records the additions, field changes and removals; the previous generation stays readable; a failed or empty re-read removes nothing.
      Leaves out: full validation suites → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Full validation suites
      Objective: Cover the historical formats and failure cases of Stages 1–5 with committed fixtures that run without SEC access.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening)
      Consumes: Stages 1–5
      Produces: a fixture-based test suite that runs in CI with no network access
      Exit: the suite passes offline over golden index files across the ingested range, malformed and HTML-error responses, interrupted downloads, and quarterly corrections; each such input fails closed or yields the expected rows.
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Scheduling and deployment
      Objective: Run daily index ingestion, and the submission and 10-K/8-K handling for new filings, unattended on a schedule, in a deployed environment.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening)
      Consumes: Stages 1–6
      Produces: a deployed, scheduled pipeline with run reports and alerts
      Exit: scheduled runs pick up each new daily index and its filings without manual steps; a missed run catches up on the next one; run reports show gaps and failures; all SEC traffic shares one request budget.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming
